title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a deliberate attempt to manipulate AI retrieval and citation behavior by flooding the web with content engineered to look like neutral academic research. The failure mode is not a flaw in any single AI model but a vulnerability in how language models and chatbots source and cite information: if content is formatted to match the queries users ask and is present at scale, systems trained or grounded on web data may treat it as credible. The operation targeted that pipeline directly, using AI optimization techniques to increase the likelihood that chatbots would surface the fabricated think tank's reports as authoritative.

The attack happened upstream of any individual AI deployment, at the data and retrieval layer rather than inside a model. Catching it would have required either source verification before ingestion, detection of coordinated inauthentic publication patterns, or human editorial review of cited sources, none of which most deployed chatbot systems perform automatically. The volume and speed of publication, 124 reports in eight days, was itself part of the strategy, designed to outpace any manual review.

What is not established is whether any specific AI system's outputs were materially altered by the operation, or whether the content was in fact incorporated into any model's training data or retrieval index. The reporting describes intent, method, and registration as a foreign agent operation, but it does not document confirmed cases of a chatbot citing the Hanover Institute's material as a result.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israeli officials established a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, funded through intermediary companies, to influence artificial intelligence systems toward pro-Israel messaging. Between August 6 and 14, the website published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to appear as neutral academic research addressing controversial topics like genocide allegations and Palestinian expulsions. The operation employed specialized AI optimization techniques to ensure chatbots would cite the content, with all reports formatted as questions users might ask AI systems. The scheme was registered with the US Justice Department as a foreign agent operation, violating transparency requirements.

The broader campaign, financed through tens of millions of dollars and coordinated by European advertising firm Havas Media, involved multiple American contractors including firms connected to former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale. Israeli government records show substantial unaccounted funding during the campaign period, while officials privately acknowledged the operation failed to improve Israel's declining public approval in America. Experts warn the project demonstrates how foreign governments increasingly manipulate AI training data and chatbot responses, a concerning development with implications beyond this specific case.
